title: NavigationServer3D.AgentGetPosition does not report the correct position in the RVO backend
body:
### Tested versions

Is reproducible in godot 4.5.1 and based on the underlying cause can traced back at least to commit a6ac305 (#69988).

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 63.90 GiB memory

### Issue description

There is an issue involving a difference between the position of an RVO agent (in the library code) and the godot agent (using its own position). I would expect the library to always provide such velocity, where if used, collision should be impossible. Whether that happens correctly or not is not exactly the point of this bug report. From the observation that either does not happen or I am doing something wrong (once again not the main point). The problem which arises is that in such circumstances (and I did not check the RVO lib code thoroughly to really pinpoint what is happening), when collision happens or I guess is inevitable, it moves one or possibly both of the agents out of the collision. Whether this is correct behavior or not I will leave up to you.

The problem is, that the changed position is not reflected in the value which _NavigationServer3D.AgentGetPosition_ provides, as it is the same value that _/modules/navigation_3d/3d/godot_navigation_server_3d.h_ returns. And as is clear from _/modules/navigation_3d/3d/godot_navigation_server_3d.cpp_ and _/modules/navigation_3d/3d/nav_map_3d.cpp_, this value is only updated from the setters (and never from the rvo simulation). This would be fine if the calculation of the 3rd party library did not move the objects. Since the position between these classes gets desynced, it can produce odd results. The only way to really see the RVO position is to do what I did in the video and "go around" the agents.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1548ce29-2a62-4440-b00f-ebde28891b65

Of course, It is possible to work around this, for example, I could set the position of the agent at every physics update, but that does not really solve the issue, merely hides it.

### Steps to reproduce

Open the attached project, make sure to let the navigation plan a path through one of the agents position or, even better, only a small part of the stationary agents. You may need to play with it a little while but after some time you should get the same result as shown in the video above.

The agents use only the RVO, no colliders are used.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mpr-rvo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25621357/mpr-rvo.zip)
